Convening governments and corporate location decision-makers

A neutral platform where destinations presented their ecosystems and companies set out their requirements.

The objective

As global brands and technology-services companies expanded their presence in India, Indian states sought to attract them, and companies needed meaningful conversations to decide where to establish operations.

Shyam’s contribution

Through his social enterprise, Shyam created a business-destination platform where state governments could showcase their ecosystems and companies could hold meaningful conversations about setting up operations.

He personally designed the engagement formats, in which government officials listened to the requirements of corporate location decision-makers and helped them set up operations. He did not lobby companies to favour one state over another; the decision was left entirely to the companies.

The outcome

Over three years, business-destination summits were held in 11 cities, each highlighting the strengths of its city. Shyam then decided to withdraw, as representing governments could conflict with the platform’s neutrality.

Source: Shyam Sundar Pani’s account.

The experience this brings

Designing neutral forums in which governments and companies can set out what each needs.
